title: Unifying Behavior Modeling and Semantic Generation for Generative Recommendation

problem.claim: Generative recommendation can favor semantically similar items while neglecting items with behavioral relevance but weak semantic similarity.

gap.claim: Existing generative recommendation methods do not seamlessly integrate behavior modeling with semantic generation.

contributions.claim: OMG unifies behavior modeling and semantic generation for recommendation.
Hybrid Behavior-Semantic Encoding captures behavioral patterns alongside semantic correlations in interaction sequences.
Behavior-Semantic Latent Reasoning iteratively transforms encoder outputs from behavioral space to semantic space to guide semantic-ID decoding.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent OMG gains over baseline methods on benchmark datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative recommendation assigns content-derived semantic IDs and generates target-item IDs from past user sessions.
Generative recommendation can exhibit semantic preference bias and miss behaviorally relevant items with weak semantic similarity.
OMG combines behavior modeling and semantic generation through hybrid encoding, latent reasoning, and behavior-reinforced generation.
The authors report consistent improvement over baseline methods on benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: Semantic similarity can cause generative recommendation to overlook behaviorally relevant items.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation systems may benefit from jointly representing semantic and behavioral signals.

application.claim: Encode interaction sequences with both behavioral and semantic information when semantic-only generation produces preference bias.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported benchmark datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results for the proposed components.
